newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Eurofighter re-enters contest of UAE fighter deal. [CORRECTED 19:56 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Eurofighter re-enters contest of UAE fighter deal. [CORRECTED 19:56 GMT]

text.p: The Eurofighter re-entered a contest to sell Abu Dhabi up to 80 warplanes, competing with original favourites Lockheed Martin and France's Dassault in the $6 billion race. (corrects from $4 billion)

The United Arab Emirates said on Monday it had received a new proposal from the partners of the Eurofighter for the UAE's warplane requirements as well as a fresh offer from Dassault Aviation for its Rafale fighter.

Speaking at a news conference at the UAE's IDEX arms show, Colonel Obeid al-Kitbi, the Gulf Arab state's deputy director general of arms procurements, said the UAE was now considering the Eurofighter along with the Rafale and Lockheed's F-16.
The news conference came after months of speculation by industry executives and analysts that Lockheed was poised to win the lion's share of the deal.
"Lockheed thought they had it clinched about 10 days ago," a Western diplomat told Reuters.

"This is really going to frustrate the Americans. The general feeling among the Americans is that they provided the UAE with all the requirements they had for the F-16," another Western diplomat said.

Lockheed officials on Sunday said the U.S. government had approved almost all of the UAE's requirements for sophisticated weaponry and systems for the F-16 and expressed hope that the green light could boost the defence giant's chances of grabbing most or all of the deal.
"This deal has been called the last of its size this century," the diplomat added. "But I think it will be the first of its size in the next century. They have been looking at proposals for years."
He said that the move was a UAE negotiating tactic.
"They probably are buying for time and trying to get the price down," the diplomat said.

The Americans have watched France secure several deals with the UAE over the past few years -- including a 1993 tank package worth $3.62 billion -- and have been seeking a foothold in the country with a healthy appetite for military hardware.

A Eurofighter deal would help Britain's bid to gain a greater market share in the Gulf, where intensive French lobbying and U.S. political credit earned in the 1991 Gulf War has squeezed Britain out of several deals, analysts say.
Eurofighter partners are British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA), Alenia Spa of Italy and Spain's CASA. Alenia is a unit of state-controlled engineering group Finmeccanica.

"It's very good news. I believe that the Eurofighter is the world's most capable affordable fighter and one of the only four fourth generation fighters in the world, so clearly it makes a lot of sense for the UAE to be including the aircraft," said Charles Masefield, head of Britain's Defence Export Services Organisation.

Kitbi said the UAE was still evaluating the existing Dassault and Lockheed proposals together with the new offers, adding that the country would evaluate all the proposals in April or May and announce a decision two to three months later.

The Eurofighter partners had originally bid for the deal, with an offer to lease Tornado aircraft ahead of the development of the Eurofighter 2000. But last year official UAE military sources said Lockheed Martin and Dassault were the only two serious contenders.
The UAE, increasingly becoming a player on the international arms market, has a requirement for multi-role, long-range aircraft with superior air-to-air- combat capability.
